entries.description: Local MCP tools for Python risk scans, protected builds, delivery inspection and traceback restoration. No source uploads or telemetry; dependency lookup is opt-in and Pro licence verification may use the network. Trial tool returns guidance only. Companion Community pre-commit hooks for mapping/private-key checks and built-output inspection are available since Core 0.13.0, via the CLI rather than MCP. Since 0.15.0, delivery inspection performs bounded top-level PyInstaller CArchive checks while leaving embedded PYZ and unrecognised member types explicitly unknown; JSON separates total, fully checked and unknown member counts. Unreleased: directory scans also inspect detected top-level PyInstaller executables, aggregate frozen counts and use <executable relative path>!<member path> finding paths; at most 32 readers share the expanded-member budget. Uninspected executables or unknown members still warn; malformed or over-limit recognised archives abort inspection. Since Core 0.14.0: CI environment-key builds require issuer-signed, request-bound admission with no unsigned fallback. The license server serves the signed endpoint; older clients keep using the legacy endpoint. Workstation and offline use are unchanged. Signed endpoint denials disable caching and hide internal inactive-state values. Since 0.15.0, clients trust a standby issuer key ahead of future rotation and report an upgrade hint for unknown issuer keys while still denying the build.
